subject: Post-demo: competitive quality handoff & prioritized next tests
messages:
From: logan_wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@novus.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga.p@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: competitive quality handoff & prioritized next tests

Maya — really appreciated you and the CloudWave team taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on what success looks like for the POC: 

Summary (from today's call)
- Primary use case: content moderation and automated summarization for developer-generated docs (high recall on unsafe content, low hallucination on summary).
- Key non-functional priorities: latency <= 180ms p50 in their EU gateway (but initial POC in us-west), strong hallucination controls for factual summaries, and predictable per-token cost.

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will deliver)
1) Side-by-side quality comparison vs CloudWave's current hyperscaler endpoint and a generic LLM endpoint (two baselines).
2) Focused eval set: 150 prompt pairs (shared in attachment) covering edge-case hallucination triggers, long-context summarization, and entity-sensitive redactions.
3) Quantitative metrics: hallucination rate, factuality score (oracle-based), p50/p95 latency, and token-cost estimate under expected QPS.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Please confirm the three business priorities above and whether we should include privacy-preserving answer masking as a criterion.
- I'll hand this to Marcus and Ben to scope the comparative tests (latency/cost + quality). Expect a proposed test plan by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: 20271208-test-prompts.csv (seed prompts), cloudwave-poc-specs.pdf (POC checklist), hallucination-sample-set.jsonl

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
logan.w@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

From: Maya Patel <maya@novus.ai>
To: logan_wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudWave Eng <eng@cloudwave.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: competitive quality handoff & prioritized next tests

Thanks Logan — good notes and yes, that matches our priorities. Two clarifications: 

1) Privacy-preserving masking: yes please include that as a soft requirement — we need to see how often the models expose PII when summarizing. It can be a secondary metric but should be present.
2) Baselines: the two baselines are our in-house hyperscaler endpoint (v2) and the public API the engineering team has been experimenting with (for reference: hp-api.example.com).

Timeline: we can allocate two engineers to collaborate (they'll be the contact for test harness integration). I'll introduce them in a follow-up note this afternoon.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Integrations, Novus (partnering with CloudWave)
maya@novus.ai

From: logan_wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga.p@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: competitive quality handoff & prioritized next tests

Team — forwarding Maya's confirmation and the POC asks. High-level handoff and priority list for the comparative evaluation we're running against CloudWave's hyperscaler and a public API. Please keep this tight and ops-ready; marketing/legal will look at the results.

Priority ranking (please scope in this order):
A) Hallucination/factuality comparison on the 150-case set (goal: show statistically significant reduction in hallucination vs hyperscaler at same latency bucket).
B) Token-cost model + p50/p95 latency under a 10 QPS synthetic workload (estimate both hosted Redwood and Dedicated extrapolation).
C) Privacy/PII leakage check — automated redaction mask tests and manual spot checks on 30 high-risk prompts.
D) Qualitative summary scoring (3 raters) for long-context summaries (>2k tokens).

Deliverables and owners: 
- Test harness + scripts (Marcus) — include direct calls to CloudWave hyperscaler and hp-api.example.com; instrument for latency and token counts.
- Prompt seeding, labeling instructions, and gold answers (Ben) — use attachment "20271208-test-prompts.csv" as base and expand to 150 pairs.
- Hallucination sample curation and manual evaluation plan (Olga) — plan to run blind review with rubric.

Constraints/notes:
- Marcus: include quantized model variants; CloudWave cares about cost impact. Also show one run with Redwood's prefix caching enabled to demonstrate cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Keep results reproducible: store outputs in the Drive link (shared in metadata).

Deadline: proposed test plan + timeline by EOD tomorrow (2027-12-09). I'll get Sales leadership approval to prioritize compute time if needed.

Logan

From: marcus_lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>
To: logan_wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga.p@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: competitive quality handoff & prioritized next tests

Quick plan and estimates:

Scope I (Hallucination/factuality run):
- Harness: will fork the existing A/B runner and add adapters for CloudWave hyperscaler and hp-api.example.com. ETA: 1 business day to stand up the adapters and test with 20 prompts.
- Compute: for full 150-case run across 3 model variants (baseline, quantized, cached), estimate 12 GPU hours on g4dn-like instances (we can run in hosted).
- Metrics: hallucination rate via string-match + human adjudication; factuality score via lookup table for entities.

Scope II (Latency/cost):
- Synthetic 10 QPS runner with 3-minute windows to capture p50/p95; will instrument token-level cost and approximate cloud outbound egress. ETA: 2 business days.

Scope III (PII leakage):
- Run automated regex checks + 30 manual spot audits (Olga to coordinate). ETA: 1 day to run, 2 days for manual review.

Attachments: plan-templates.zip (contains adapter README, runner config), preliminary-cost-estimates.csv

I'll start today on the A/B adapter. Ben — can you finalize the expanded prompt set and gold answers? Olga — confirm raters and rubric by EOD.

— Marcus
